newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees room for just one European plane-maker.
newsitem.headline: France sees room for just one European plane-maker.

text.p: New French Defence Minister Alain Richard was quoted on Thursday as saying there was room for just one plane-maker in Europe and that he saw a combined Dassault-Aerospatiale as simply a component of such a firm.

In testimony to the National Assembly committee on Defence delivered on Wednesday and made public a day later, Richard added that the situation was different for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, which he said was important enough not to have to be submerged into a conglomerate.
"In the aerospace industry, it seems a given that there is room for just one plane-maker, civilian and military, in Europe," Richard told the assembly committee.
"Negotiations in search of agreements with the governments of other countries are fundamental, with the bringing together of Dassault and Aerospatiale a simple component," he said.

But in the defence electronics sector, he said it was not clear that just a single European firm was required and added: "The position occupied by Thomson-CSF makes it big enough not to have to be a secondary player."

European and U.S. aerospace executives have been anxious to know the new leftist government's plans for defence industry consolidation. The previous centre-right government's plans to privatise state-owned Thomson-CSF and merge Dassault and Aerospatiale were seen as keys to unlock further European defence consolidation, needed to face up to competition from mega-mergers in the United States.
